answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identities to boundary-layer scintillometry. Nodes authenticate by measuring optical turbulence from a coastal zephyr passing an instrumented wharf at the diurnal thermal nadir. An attacker must maintain discrete line-of-sight laser transceivers per identity, incurring substantial hardware and real-estate costs. However, dense coastal fog attenuates optical paths, periodically causing false rejections.
